lyrics:
[Intro: relaxed disco bass line, soft strings, finger snaps]

[Verse 1: low, husky, unhurried]
We were a postcard, we were a view
A dinner party's favourite two
Built a place and watched it sell
Mm, we wished each other well

[Pre-Chorus: strings rise, voice lifts a little]
I didn't want to go, I didn't want to stay
I sat a while, and then I found a way

[Chorus: steady groove, calm, doubled voice]
I can book a table for one
Window seat, the good red, the long lunch
I can order both desserts
Laugh at my own jokes until it hurts
I can walk me home
I know the way
I can love me fine on a weekday

[Verse 2: low, a little brighter]
Painted the bedroom the colour you hated
Kept the dog and the chair, donated
The rest, and I learned how the boiler works
Mm, it has its quirks

[Pre-Chorus: strings rise, voice lifts a little]
I didn't want to go, I didn't want to stay
I sat a while, and then I found a way

[Chorus: steady groove, calm, doubled voice]
I can book a table for one
Window seat, the good red, the long lunch
I can order both desserts
Laugh at my own jokes until it hurts
I can walk me home
I know the way
I can love me fine on a weekday

[Bridge: bass and snaps only, voice close]
I didn't want to learn this
I'm glad I did
I didn't want to learn this

[Final Chorus: fullest, strings soaring, voice opens]
I can book a table for one
Window seat, the good red, the long lunch
I can order both desserts
Laugh at my own jokes until it hurts
I can walk me home
I know the way
I can love me fine on a weekday

[Outro: bass line, a glass set down, soft laugh]
Table for one, please
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 118 BPM, 4/4, A minor. A relaxed, steady disco walk. Composed, warm and a little rueful.

VOICE: Female alto, low, husky and grainy, with a country-rock edge. She sings well within herself for most of the song, almost conversational, and opens up only in the last chorus. Doubled in the choruses. A soft 'mm' between lines.

INSTRUMENTS: A round, melodic electric bass playing a relaxed disco line. A steady four-on-the-floor kick with a soft snare. A string section. Clean, muted rhythm guitar. Finger snaps. Electric piano. Light congas.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, bass, strings and snaps. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:33 Pre-chorus. 0:45 Chorus 1. 1:14 Verse 2. 1:35 Pre-chorus. 1:47 Chorus 2. 2:16 Bridge, bass and snaps. 2:32 Final chorus, with the voice at its fullest. 3:01 Outro, the bass line, a glass set down, a laugh and a spoken line at 3:12.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2020s soft disco: warm, clean and uncluttered, bass and voice at the front, strings wide.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The bass line alone under the first words.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The independence is domestic and specific: a boiler learned, a bedroom repainted, a weekday lunch. The bridge is honest that she did not want the lesson, which keeps it from being a slogan.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Fond memory, steadiness, admission, contentment.
